_comment: The keys this project holds, by PUBLIC half, and what each one can do. Secrets are never here and never in git — *.key is ignored. A label is a claim about custody, so each entry says where the secret lives and how the public half can be re-derived, because an inventory that merely asserts 'this is the principal' is worth nothing. sdk/tools/keys.ts reads this to label its report; a key with no entry is shown as a bare key, which is the honest rendering of one nobody has accounted for.
_the_three_powers: agentKey spends inside the limits. revocationKey stops a grant at any moment and receives NOTHING. principalKey receives the balance on revoke or reclaim. `revoke` pays the principal rather than its own signer on purpose, so a monitor can be trusted to stop a grant without being trusted with its balance — which is only true when they are different keys.

keys.label: funder, and principal of every grant issued so far
keys.secretLives: warda-testnet.key, on the machine that runs the agents
keys.derivation: the x-only public key of warda-testnet.key; it appears as `principal` and `revocation` in every manifest under x402/demo/
can: create grants — genesis spends this key's coin
receive the balance of any grant on revoke or reclaim
stop any grant issued so far, because it is also their revocation key
keys.shouldBe: three keys, not one. On mainnet the principal must be generated offline on a machine that never runs an agent, and genesis now refuses principal == revocation there.

keys.label: revocation key, for grants issued from here on
keys.derivation: generated by sdk/tools/new-key.ts on 16 September 2026; address kaspatest:qpxrv3pwa8ckw7sycu4jnyc6rza7ppd5fwed59j6jed5mx73l3yfw2x2nvkag
can: stop any grant that names it, at any moment, without the agent's agreement
receive NOTHING — a revoke pays the principal, so this key cannot move a balance anywhere but home
keys.shouldBe: used as --revocation on every new grant. It is deliberately allowed to be warmer than the principal: that asymmetry is the whole reason the two roles exist.
keys.usedBy: grant-006, issued 17 September 2026 — the first grant whose revocation key is not its principal. It was used in anger the same day: the first issue of #006 was revoked with it (0528e87665208acd68068cd4b19051fbe702596036b8390bcc1f3bc2d6e7f690) and the balance went home to the principal, which is the asymmetry working. Grants issued before it hash their keys into their address and cannot adopt it.

keys.label: funder, and principal of grant-006
keys.secretLives: funder.key, in ~/Desktop/warda-agent-006 on the machine that runs the agents — NOT in this repo, and not the same file as covenant/deploy/warda-testnet.key. agent-006/ in this repo holds that agent's manifest and records only.
keys.derivation: the x-only public key of that funder.key; address kaspatest:qplutjmzldzj9tphlzg2tj200c3ldle078fqzum535nu95sz69g3yucfaklyp, recorded as fundingAddress in agent-006/funding.json and as `principal` in agent-006/grant-006.json
can: create grants — genesis spends this key's coin
receive the balance of grant-006 on revoke or reclaim
keys.bornOf: a mistake worth keeping in the record: on 17 September 2026 a re-run of a pasted block called `warda key` again, and new-key.ts wrote over the funder key it found, stranding the coin at the address the old one controlled. new-key.ts and quickstart.ts now refuse to overwrite a key file, and ops/check-key-writes.mjs makes that refusal a rule rather than a habit. This key is the replacement.
keys.shouldBe: retired in favour of a principal generated offline, once anything here runs on mainnet. It is a funder that also receives, which is two of the three powers in one file.
